headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors if CrewAI ingests untrusted content from the knowledge list; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list with no execution surface, while CrewAI reads files and stdin/stdout and can use shared working-directory content. That creates a plausible path where untrusted list entries or copied content are treated as instructions. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, so uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF CrewAI ingests content copied from the knowledge list as instructions without provenance checks
IF both agents share a writable workspace or clipboard bridge
mitigations: Treat list content as data only, not instructions
Add a provenance tag to any imported snippets
Disable automatic tool execution on parsed text
Run CrewAI in a separate container
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not a meaningful source of leakage. CrewAI can read the host working directory and send context to model providers or configured tools, so leakage is possible only if sensitive files are placed in that workspace. The blast radius is limited by the empty data profile on agent_a.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in CrewAI's working directory
IF CrewAI is configured with external model providers or tools that transmit context
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the working directory
Use a dedicated non-sensitive workspace
Rotate or scope API keys narrowly
Review tool integrations before enabling them
requires-engineering: add workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, so it cannot conflict directly. CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and its concurrency model allows multiple instances with developer-defined shared state. If the pair is orchestrated around a shared directory, CrewAI instances can race with each other even though agent_a itself cannot write.
conditions: IF multiple CrewAI instances share the same writable working directory
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking around shared state
mitigations: Assign each instance a separate workspace
Disable shared-state reuse
Add file locks around writes
Avoid concurrent writes to the same artifacts
requires-engineering: implement orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted can supply curated links or descriptions that CrewAI may treat as authoritative input, while CrewAI can act on tool outputs and write files. There is no verification mechanism in either profile that guarantees downstream checking, so a bad or stale entry can cascade into incorrect actions or generated artifacts. The interaction is plausible but not inherently irreversible.
conditions: IF CrewAI uses entries from the knowledge list as authoritative facts
IF downstream tools or agents act on those facts without verification
mitigations: Require source verification before action
Mark imported entries as untrusted
Add a human review step for high-impact outputs
Log provenance for every derived claim
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data classes are identified for awesome-selfhosted, so compliance exposure from agent_a is minimal. CrewAI can handle developer-passed data and API keys, which can create policy mismatch only if regulated data is injected into its workspace or tools. Because the sensitive class is not present by default, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is passed into CrewAI
IF CrewAI tools or model providers are outside the required compliance boundary
mitigations: Do not pass regulated data into the crew
Use a compliance-approved provider set
Separate secrets from task content
Document retention and deletion handling
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data classes
